intro.say: Let's learn how washing hands keeps us healthy!

rounds.say: Germs are tiny living things. They are so small we can't see them! Some germs can make us sick.
rounds.caption: Germs are tiny

rounds.say: Soap and water wash germs off our hands. Wash before you eat and after you use the toilet.
rounds.caption: Soap + water

rounds.ask: What do we use to wash germs away?

options.label: Chocolate
options.why: Chocolate makes hands sticky!

options.label: Crayons
options.why: Crayons are for drawing.

rounds.explain: Soap and water wash germs off.

rounds.ask: Can you see germs with just your eyes?

options.label: Yes
options.why: They are much too tiny to see.

rounds.explain: Germs are so tiny, you need a microscope to see them.

rounds.ask: When should you wash your hands?

options.label: Watching TV
options.why: Washing then is fine, but there is a more important time.

options.label: While sleeping
options.why: You can't wash while asleep!

rounds.explain: Wash before eating so germs do not go in your mouth.

rounds.ask: You just used the toilet. What now?

options.label: Run off
options.why: Wait! Germs are still on your hands.

options.label: Eat a cookie
options.why: Wash first!

rounds.explain: Always wash your hands after using the toilet.

rounds.ask: Do you need to wash your hands now?
rounds.explain: Wash after the toilet, after pets, and before food.

intro.say: Germs can jump from person to person. Let's learn how to stop them!

rounds.say: When you sneeze or cough, tiny drops fly out with germs inside. Cover your mouth with a tissue or your elbow.
rounds.caption: Cover sneezes

rounds.say: Throw the tissue in the bin, then wash your hands. Now the germs can't spread to your friends!
rounds.caption: Bin it, then wash

rounds.ask: You need to sneeze! What should you do?

options.label: Sneeze on friend
options.why: That spreads germs to your friend.

options.label: Sneeze in hand, no wash
options.why: Germs stay on your hand.

rounds.explain: Sneezing into a tissue or your elbow keeps germs from flying.

rounds.ask: What do you do with a used tissue?

options.label: Put in pocket
options.why: Germs would stay in your pocket.

options.label: Give to friend
options.why: That would pass on germs.

rounds.explain: Put used tissues in the bin straight away.

rounds.ask: How long should you scrub with soap?

options.label: One second
options.why: That is too quick.

options.label: One hour
options.why: That is far too long!

rounds.explain: Scrub for about 20 seconds, like singing happy birthday twice.

rounds.ask: Which hand is ready to eat a snack?

options.label: Muddy hands
options.why: Muddy hands carry germs.

rounds.explain: Clean, washed hands are ready for food.

rounds.ask: Put the hand washing steps in order.
rounds.explain: Wet, soap, scrub, rinse and dry.

intro.say: Let's think like germ detectives and find the smartest ways to stay healthy.

rounds.say: Germs love warm, wet and dirty places. They can sit on door handles, toys and phones, then hop onto hands.
rounds.caption: Germs hide on things

rounds.say: Not all germs are bad, but washing, covering coughs, and keeping things clean stops the ones that make us sick.
rounds.caption: Clean = healthy

rounds.ask: Why does soap work better than water alone?

options.label: Soap has colours
options.why: Colours do not clean.

options.label: Soap smells nice
options.why: The smell does not remove germs.

rounds.explain: Soap grabs germs and dirt so water can wash them away.

rounds.ask: Leo has a cold. What is the kindest thing to do?

options.label: Share his cup
options.why: Sharing cups spreads germs.

options.label: Hug everyone
options.why: Hugs can pass his germs on.

rounds.explain: Resting and covering coughs keeps friends from catching it.

rounds.ask: Where might lots of germs hide?

options.label: The sun
options.why: Germs can't live on the sun!

options.label: A star
options.why: Stars are far away in space.

rounds.explain: Many hands touch door handles, so germs collect there.

rounds.ask: Why should you not touch your eyes, nose or mouth with dirty hands?

options.label: It tickles
options.why: There is a more important reason.

options.label: It leaves colour
options.why: Germs are invisible, not colourful.

rounds.explain: Germs can get into your body through your eyes, nose and mouth.

rounds.ask: Ava touched a door handle, then wants a sandwich. What first?

options.label: Eat now
options.why: Germs from the handle could go in her mouth.

options.label: Wipe on shirt
options.why: That moves germs onto the shirt.

rounds.explain: Washing first gets rid of germs from the handle.

rounds.ask: Does this help stop germs, or spread germs?
rounds.explain: Washing, binning and cleaning stop germs, sharing cups and sneezing on people spread them.
